objective: Add the budget, one-attempt identity and reservation rules for AI-generated covers.
deliverable: Reviewable pull request with passing tests; no merge or deployment.
requirements: Create src/lib/ai-cover-budget.ts exactly as specified in the acceptance test header, following the existing description budget pattern in src/lib/description-generation.ts (atomic DynamoDB TransactWriteItems, one deterministic attempt per owner, item and style, no retries).
Import from the existing module with an explicit extension (import ... from "./ai-cover.ts") so Node tests can load it, as src/lib/description-http.ts does. Use node:crypto for SHA-256.
This module only builds data structures: it must not import AWS SDKs, Supabase or React, and must not perform network, file or environment access.
src/lib/ai-cover.ts is provided for reference and must not be changed; its existing acceptance tests must keep passing.
Owner budget: US$2.00 total with a US$0.05 reservation per image (list price US$0.04), at most 40 generations.

Division of checks: coverBudgetAvailability validates value types (safe integers, ranges) of the stored record; the DynamoDB ConditionExpression enforces the same rules as comparisons (app_enabled = true, exact app_version, app_commit and limit_micro_usd, reserved_micro_usd <= limit minus one reservation, dispatches < app_dispatch_limit, app_dispatch_limit <= AI_COVER_MAX_DISPATCHES, app_expires_at > now). DynamoDB conditions cannot test whether a number is an integer; the owner writes the budget record with integers, so fractional stored values are out of scope for the condition and not a defect.
Keep the change small: one module and one focused test file; a repair should change only what its findings require.
acceptance_tests_note: Factory-owned tests run unchanged in the sandbox after the repository checks, together with the existing ai-cover acceptance tests; the builder cannot edit them and must make them pass.
source_manifest_note: Computed by the coding assistant from a separate read-only clone with both the Factory reader and the owner's standalone script (110 files, 692540 bytes); the Factory fetch verifies it independently before use.
